title: Seconds Calculator
story: Your friend says they've been alive for about 15 years. You pause, do some quick mental math, and say: 'That's over 473 million seconds!' Their jaw drops. Let's build a program that does this instantly.
why: Chaining multiplication with variables is a practical way to understand how compound calculations work — from seconds to days to years.
analogy: Time calculations are like stacking building blocks — each layer (minutes, hours, days) builds on top of the one before it.
try_it: Add `day_per_year: Int = 365` and calculate seconds in a year. Then try calculating how many seconds YOU have been alive!
tips: Chain your calculations — each result feeds into the next, making your code clean and logical
Use descriptive variable names like `sec_per_day` so anyone reading your code instantly understands
Print every step so you can verify each calculation is correct
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply ALL the factors — seconds in a day is 60 × 60 × 24, not just 60 × 24
Using the wrong unit — make sure you're multiplying seconds by minutes, not seconds by seconds
